acceptance_criteria.criterion: All routing decisions are delegated to ledger_get_next_action
Supervisor correctly routes IMPLEMENT, REWORK, RUN_QA, REWORK_QA, RUN_REVIEW, WRITE_DOCS, FINALIZE_WP, UPDATE_CRITERIA to correct stages
Supervisor correctly routes RESUME_OR_CANCEL, CONTINUE_PIPELINE, BLOCK_FOR_REWORK_LIMIT, REPAIR_ORPHAN_BLOCKED
PM actions (UNBLOCK_WP, REVIEW_REWORK_LIMIT, REVIEW_STALE, REVIEW_ABANDONED) route to pm stage
Unrecognised action strings are treated as WAIT with warning log
Circuit breaker skips WPs with 3 or more consecutive failures
All roles returning WAIT routes to synthesis
ledger_get_project_status and ledger_list_work_packages calls retained for observability
Existing tests in orchestrator/tests/ pass without regression

summary: Removed _get_latest_pipeline, _route_for_wp, and _SKIP_IN_FLIGHT from supervisor.py.
Added _SKIP_ACTIONS, _DISPATCH_ACTIONS, _ROLE_STAGE_MAP module-level constants.
Replaced hardcoded WP routing loop with ledger_get_next_action per-role loop.
All 5 roles queried in order; first dispatchable action wins.
Circuit breaker (3 consecutive failures) preserved.
Updated test_supervisor.py with _derive_next_action mock helper and ledger_get_next_action tool.
Updated test_integration.py ScriptedLedger to include ledger_get_next_action mock.
Updated 4 behavior-changed tests (all-blocked->pm, in-flight->continue, circuit-broken->synthesis).
162 tests pass, 1 skipped.

comments.note: The behavior change from 'all blocked -> END' to 'all blocked -> pm (REPAIR_ORPHAN_BLOCKED)' and from 'in-flight-only -> END' to 'in-flight -> developer (CONTINUE_PIPELINE)' are intentional improvements aligned with the MCP server's richer decision logic. Tests updated to reflect new behavior.
The _derive_next_action helper in test files replicates routing logic. It could live in a shared test utility module to avoid duplication between test_supervisor.py and test_integration.py.

summary: All 10 ACs verified. _route_for_wp, _get_latest_pipeline, and _SKIP_IN_FLIGHT are fully removed.
_SKIP_ACTIONS, _DISPATCH_ACTIONS, and _ROLE_STAGE_MAP module-level constants correctly implement the routing table. Unrecognised actions treated as WAIT with warning.
Circuit breaker (3 consecutive failures), ledger_get_project_status, and ledger_list_work_packages calls all retained.
162 tests passed, 1 skipped, 0 failures.

comments.note: BLOCK_FOR_REWORK_LIMIT is correctly in _SKIP_ACTIONS (not a dispatch), as expected — it's a 'circuit breaker triggered' signal from the server, not a task to hand off. REPAIR_ORPHAN_BLOCKED is correctly a PM dispatch. The _derive_next_action test helper duplicates routing logic; lower-priority refactor opportunity to consolidate into a shared test utility.

summary: Excellent refactoring. _SKIP_ACTIONS, _DISPATCH_ACTIONS, and _ROLE_STAGE_MAP module-level constants are clean, readable, and easy to extend.
Delegation of all routing decisions to ledger_get_next_action is architecturally sound — the MCP server is the authoritative routing source.
Forward-compatibility guard (unrecognised actions treated as WAIT with warning) is the correct defensive pattern for evolving server vocabularies.
Circuit breaker (consecutive >= 3) is correctly scoped: fires per-WP, skips but continues to check other WPs/roles, and records errors for observability.
_call_tool correctly handles both list[TextBlock] and string response shapes from langchain-mcp-adapters.
Non-blocking: REWORK_QA is dead code in _DISPATCH_ACTIONS (removed from MCP server in prior audit). Non-blocking: _ROLES priority order should carry a comment to prevent accidental reordering.
No blocking issues found.

comments.note: Non-blocking: REWORK_QA is present in _DISPATCH_ACTIONS but the MCP server no longer emits it (removed in the workflow-specification-audit-fixes2 project). It's dead code. Consider removing it from _DISPATCH_ACTIONS in a future cleanup to keep the routing table in sync with actual server behavior.

Non-blocking: The _ROLES list ordering (Project Manager, Developer, QA, Reviewer, Documentation) encodes an implicit dispatch priority. A short comment explaining the intent would prevent accidental reordering in future maintenance.

The extra_errors list accumulation pattern is correct: halted-WP errors are surfaced on every Command regardless of final routing destination (early-return or fall-through), ensuring observability even when the circuit breaker skips a WP but another WP IS dispatched.

summary: Rewrote the Supervisor (deterministic router) subsection in Architecture: updated the description to document delegation to ledger_get_next_action as the authoritative routing source; replaced the stale pipeline-state-machine routing table with an action-based table matching _DISPATCH_ACTIONS.

Rewrote Special Exits: added pre-loop checks ('no WPs → pm', 'all terminal → synthesis') that were missing; removed the inaccurate 'circuit-breaker → __end__' exit (circuit-breaker now skips WPs and falls through to synthesis).
Rewrote Standard Routing block: replaced the hardcoded per-WP pipeline state machine with the new role-priority dispatch model showing _SKIP_ACTIONS, _DISPATCH_ACTIONS, and _ROLE_STAGE_MAP clearly.
Fixed Circuit-Breaker subsection: updated the final sentence to accurately reflect that circuit-broken WPs fall through to synthesis rather than routing to __end__.
Removed REWORK_DOCS from the architecture table since it is not in _DISPATCH_ACTIONS and would be treated as WAIT.
All 10 acceptance criteria were already marked met by the QA and code-review pipelines.

comments.note: This was the most significant README change in this project. The supervisor's routing model changed fundamentally: from a hardcoded per-WP pipeline state machine to a role-based delegation via ledger_get_next_action. Three sections required rewriting: (1) Supervisor description paragraph (new delegation model), (2) Special Exits (added pre-loop exits for no-WPs and all-terminal), (3) Standard Routing block (replaced pipeline state machine with role-based dispatch table). Also corrected: REWORK_DOCS is NOT in _DISPATCH_ACTIONS and is treated as WAIT, so it was removed from the routing table.

The architecture routing table in the Supervisor section was simplified: old rows like 'Any pipeline IN_PROGRESS → skip' and 'All WPs BLOCKED → END' are replaced with accurate action-based rows. The 'All WPs BLOCKED → END' behavior no longer holds — orphaned blocked WPs now route to pm via REPAIR_ORPHAN_BLOCKED.
